name: Chat history search
summary: Nothing matched at three characters either. Identical to the two-letter empty state but for the query, which is the point: the copy does not react to length.

looseEnds.title: The correction is applied but never announced
looseEnds.detail: The spell-check frame searches for “medications” while the field still reads “mdeications”, and nothing on screen says a correction happened. The user cannot tell these are not results for what they typed, and has no way back to the literal query.
looseEnds.ask: Add a line naming the spelling used, with a way to search the original instead — or state that silent correction is intended.

looseEnds.title: Nothing marks the threshold between the bands
looseEnds.detail: One letter is inert, two letters fire a query. The screens differ only in the query text, so the rule lives in the frame names rather than in anything drawn. A developer reading the screens alone cannot tell where the cut is.
looseEnds.ask: Confirm the threshold is two characters, and whether a two-letter whole-word match (BP, ER) is in or out for MVP.

looseEnds.title: No cancelled or dismissed state is drawn
looseEnds.detail: Cancel sits in the bar on every frame and no frame shows what it returns to. The keyboard is up in all eight, so the list-with-keyboard-dismissed case is undrawn too.
looseEnds.ask: Does Cancel clear the query and stay, or leave search entirely?
